## DEXSeq Analysis - GSE173955

### 1. Load Required Libraries and Data

Load the core R packages required for data wrangling (`tidyverse`), differential isoform usage testing (`DEXSeq`) and parallel computation (`BiocParallel`).

```{r}
library(DEXSeq)
library(tidyverse)
library(BiocParallel)

BPPARAM_GSE173955 <- MulticoreParam(workers = 4)
out_dir_GSE173955 <- file.path("results", "DEXSeqGSE173955")
dir.create(out_dir_GSE173955, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

Load the course helper environment (`exam_functions.Rdata`), the transcript-level estimated count matrix for **GSE173955** (n=18 samoples, with Ensembl transcript IDs as rows and GEO sample accessions as columns), the cleaned sample metadata, and the official GRCh38.107 `transcript_id`-to-`gene_id` annotation table.

```{r}
load(file = "/home/projects/22140/exam_data/exam_functions.Rdata")

if (file.exists("data/processed/GSE173955/isoform_counts.rds")) {
  isoform_counts_GSE173955 <- readRDS("data/processed/GSE173955/isoform_counts.rds")
} else {
  isoform_counts_GSE173955 <- loadIsoformCountMatrix("GSE173955")
}

metadata_GSE173955 <- readr::read_csv("data/metadata/GSE173955_metadata_clean.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

tx2gene_df_GSE173955 <- readr::read_rds(
  "/home/projects/22140/exam_data/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.107.chr_patch_hapl_scaff_tx_info.Rds"
) |> 
  dplyr::select(transcript_id, gene_id) |> 
  dplyr::distinct(transcript_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

### 2. Preprocessing, Filtering & DEXSeq Model Fitting

Round estimated transcript counts to integers as required by `DEXSeq`'s negative binomial model, verify exact sample order alignment against `sample_id`, and build `sample_data` with explicit factors for `sample`, `condition` (`Control` as reference), `sex`, and z-score standardized `age_scaled`.

```{r}
# prepare integer count matrix and align sample metadata
count_matrix_GSE173955 <- round(as.matrix(isoform_counts_GSE173955))

# align metadata rows to match count matrix column order
stopifnot(all(colnames(count_matrix_GSE173955) %in% metadata_GSE173955$sample_id))
metadata_GSE173955 <- metadata_GSE173955[match(colnames(count_matrix_GSE173955), metadata_GSE173955$sample_id), ]

sample_data_GSE173955 <- data.frame(
  row.names = metadata_GSE173955$sample_id,
  sample = factor(metadata_GSE173955$sample_id),
  condition = factor(metadata_GSE173955$condition, levels = c("Control", "AD")),
  sex = factor(tolower(metadata_GSE173955$sex)),
  age_scaled = as.numeric(scale(metadata_GSE173955$age))
)
```

Align the count matrix one-to-one with the `tx2gene` annotation table and filter the feature space to retain only multi-isoform genes (`>= 2` transcripts per gene, as single-isoform genes cannot undergo differential isoform usage) and transcripts with sufficient expression (`>= 10` counts in at least 3 samples).

```{r}
# align transcript-to-gene annotation 1-to-1 and filter features
tx2gene_GSE173955 <- tx2gene_df_GSE173955 |> 
  dplyr::filter(transcript_id %in% rownames(count_matrix_GSE173955)) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(match(transcript_id, rownames(count_matrix_GSE173955)))

count_matrix_GSE173955 <- count_matrix_GSE173955[tx2gene_GSE173955$transcript_id, ]

# keep only multi-isoform genes
multi_iso_genes_GSE173955 <- tx2gene_GSE173955 |> 
  dplyr::count(gene_id) |> 
  dplyr::filter(n >= 2) |> 
  dplyr::pull(gene_id)

keep_tx_GSE173955 <- tx2gene_GSE173955$gene_id %in% multi_iso_genes_GSE173955
count_matrix_GSE173955 <- count_matrix_GSE173955[keep_tx_GSE173955, ]
tx2gene_GSE173955 <- tx2gene_GSE173955[keep_tx_GSE173955, ]

# filter low-count isoforms
keep_expr_GSE173955 <- rowSums(count_matrix_GSE173955 >= 10) >= 3
count_matrix_GSE173955 <- count_matrix_GSE173955[keep_expr_GSE173955, ]
tx2gene_GSE173955 <- tx2gene_GSE173955[keep_expr_GSE173955, ]
```

Construct the `DEXSeqDataSet` object using the covariate-adjusted interaction formula `~ sample + exon + sex:exon + age_scaled:exon + condition:exon` (where `exon` represents individual transcript features within each gene).

```{r}
# build DEXSeqDataSet object including sex and age confounders
dxd_GSE173955 <- DEXSeqDataSet(
  countData = count_matrix_GSE173955,
  sampleData = sample_data_GSE173955,
  design = ~ sample + exon + sex:exon + age_scaled:exon + condition:exon,
  featureID = tx2gene_GSE173955$transcript_id,
  groupID = tx2gene_GSE173955$gene_id
)
```

Execute the `DEXSeq` statistical workflow: estimate library size factors (`estimateSizeFactors`), fit feature dispersions (`estimateDispersions`), and test for Differential Isoform Usage via a likelihood ratio test comparing `fullModel` (`~ sample + exon + sex:exon + age_scaled:exon + condition:exon`) against `reducedModel` (`~ sample + exon + sex:exon + age_scaled:exon`) in `testForDEU()`. Finally,estimate condition-specific isoform fold changes (`estimateExonFoldChanges`) and extract `DEXSeqResults()`.

```{r}
# run DEXSeq pipeline
dxd_GSE173955 <- estimateSizeFactors(dxd_GSE173955)
dxd_GSE173955 <- estimateDispersions(dxd_GSE173955, BPPARAM = BPPARAM_GSE173955)

dxd_GSE173955 <- testForDEU(
  dxd_GSE173955,
  fullModel = ~ sample + exon + sex:exon + age_scaled:exon + condition:exon,
  reducedModel = ~ sample + exon + sex:exon + age_scaled:exon,
  BPPARAM = BPPARAM_GSE173955
)

dxd_GSE173955 <- estimateExonFoldChanges(dxd_GSE173955, fitExpToVar = "condition", BPPARAM = BPPARAM_GSE173955)
dxr_GSE173955 <- DEXSeqResults(dxd_GSE173955)
```

### 3. Extract Isoform-Level and Gene-Level Results

Extract all tested isoforms and filter significant transcripts (`padj < 0.05`). To enable gene-level comparison with `DESeq2` and preserve the test statistic (`stat`) for downstream Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (`fgseaMultilevel`), collapse results to one row per gene by selecting the isoform with the smallest raw `pvalue` (`slice_min`) and recalculating gene-level FDR across unique genes (`p.adjust(pvalue, method = "fdr")`). Save all full and significant tables as `.csv` files alongside the serialized `dxr` `.rds` object.

```{r}
# extract isoform-level and collapsed gene-level results
alpha_GSE173955 <- 0.05

res_isoforms_GSE173955 <- as.data.frame(dxr_GSE173955) |> 
  tibble::as_tibble() |> 
  dplyr::arrange(padj)

sig_isoforms_GSE173955 <- res_isoforms_GSE173955 |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj), padj < alpha_GSE173955)

lfc_col_GSE173955 <- grep("^log2fold_", colnames(res_isoforms_GSE173955), value = TRUE)[1]

# collapse to gene-level keeping the most significant isoform per gene (preserves stat & log2FC for fgsea)
res_genes_GSE173955 <- res_isoforms_GSE173955 |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(stat)) |> 
  dplyr::select(
    gene_id = groupID,
    isoform_id = featureID,
    stat,
    log2FC = dplyr::all_of(lfc_col_GSE173955),
    pvalue,
    padj
  ) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(gene_id) |> 
  dplyr::slice_min(order_by = pvalue, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> 
  dplyr::ungroup() |> 
  dplyr::mutate(padj = p.adjust(pvalue, method = "fdr")) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(padj)

sig_genes_GSE173955 <- res_genes_GSE173955 |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj), padj < alpha_GSE173955)

# summary
cat("Significant isoforms (FDR < 0.05):", nrow(sig_isoforms_GSE173955), "\n")
cat("Unique genes from significant isoforms:", length(unique(sig_isoforms_GSE173955$groupID)), "\n")
cat("Significant genes after gene-level FDR:", nrow(sig_genes_GSE173955), "\n")

# save results to results/DEXSeqGSE173955
readr::write_csv(res_isoforms_GSE173955, file.path(out_dir_GSE173955, "DEXSeq_all_isoforms_GSE173955.csv"))
readr::write_csv(sig_isoforms_GSE173955, file.path(out_dir_GSE173955, "DEXSeq_sig_isoforms_GSE173955.csv"))
readr::write_csv(res_genes_GSE173955, file.path(out_dir_GSE173955, "DEXSeq_all_genes_GSE173955.csv"))
readr::write_csv(sig_genes_GSE173955, file.path(out_dir_GSE173955, "DEXSeq_sig_genes_GSE173955.csv"))
saveRDS(dxr_GSE173955, file.path(out_dir_GSE173955, "dxr_GSE173955.rds"))
```

At the transcript level, **25 isoforms** (across **25 unique genes**) pass the genome-wide significance threshold (FDR\<0.05) when correcting simultaneously across all tested transcripts. After collapsing to one lead isoform per gene and recalculating FDR across the smaller universe of multi-isoform genes, **197 genes** exhibit statistically significant differential isoform usage (FDRgene \<0.05).

Display the top 10 genes ranked by gene-level significance, showing each gene's lead isoform (`isoform_id`), likelihood ratio statistic (`stat`), estimated `log2FC`, raw `pvalue`, and gene-level `padj`.

```{r}
# Inspect top 10 significant genes
head(res_genes_GSE173955, 10)
```

## Graphs and Analysis

Plot per-feature dispersion estimates against the mean of normalized counts to verify that `DEXSeq` accurately models biological and technical variance across expression levels.

```{r}
# 1. Dispersion estimation plot
plotDispEsts(dxd_GSE173955, main = "DEXSeq - Dispersion Estimation (GSE173955)")
```

The dispersion diagnostic plot confirms a well-behaved negative binomial fit: individual isoform dispersion estimates (black dots) follow a smooth, monotonically decreasing trend (red curve), and empirical Bayes shrinkage pulls noisy estimates toward the fitted line to produce well-calibrated final dispersions (blue dots) without distortion at low count ranges.

Generate an MA plot displaying log2 isoform usage fold changes against mean normalized expression across all tested transcripts, highlighting statistically significant isoforms (FDR\<0.05) in red.

```{r}
# 2. MA plot
plotMA(dxr_GSE173955, cex = 0.8, alpha = 0.05, main = "MA Plot - Differential Isoform Usage (GSE173955)")
```

The MA plot displays a symmetric funnel centered around log2 FC=0, where fold-change variance narrows progressively as mean normalized expression increases, and statistically significant isoforms (red) occur across moderate-to-high expression levels rather than noisy low-count transcripts.

Visualize statistical significance (−log10 (padj)) against magnitude and direction of isoform usage change (log2 FC), highlighting isoforms with increased relative usage (`padj < 0.05` and log2 FC\>0, orange) and decreased relative usage (`padj < 0.05` and log2 FC\<0, blue). The horizontal axis is restricted to \[−10,10\] via `coord_cartesian()` so that extreme unshrunken boundary estimates from zero-count groups (≈±15–20) do not compress the primary biological distribution.

```{r}
# 3. Volcano plot (adjusted for DEXSeq: FDR < 0.05 and zoomed to [-10, 10])
volcano_df_GSE173955 <- res_isoforms_GSE173955 |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj), !is.na(.data[[lfc_col_GSE173955]])) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    sig = dplyr::case_when(
      padj < 0.05 & .data[[lfc_col_GSE173955]] > 0 ~ "Increased usage (padj < 0.05)",
      padj < 0.05 & .data[[lfc_col_GSE173955]] < 0 ~ "Decreased usage (padj < 0.05)",
      TRUE ~ "Not significant"
    )
  )

volcano_plot_GSE173955 <- ggplot(
  volcano_df_GSE173955,
  aes(x = .data[[lfc_col_GSE173955]], y = -log10(padj), color = sig)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Increased usage (padj < 0.05)" = "#D55E00",
    "Decreased usage (padj < 0.05)" = "#0072B2",
    "Not significant" = "grey75"
  )) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-10, 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Differential Isoform Usage - GSE173955",
    x = paste0("Log2 Fold Change (", lfc_col_GSE173955, ")"),
    y = "-Log10 Adjusted P-value",
    color = "State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

volcano_plot_GSE173955
ggsave(file.path(out_dir_GSE173955, "volcano_plot_GSE173955.png"), plot = volcano_plot_GSE173955, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

The volcano plot highlights all significant isoforms above the dashed threshold line (FDR=0.05) across both increased and decreased relative usage in `AD`. Several top-ranked isoforms share a flat upper ceiling near −log10 (padj)≈2.40 (padj≈0.004) because Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment enforces monotonicity across closely spaced raw p-values (1.22×10−7 to 2.55×10−7).

For every gene with at least one significant isoform (FDR\<0.05), compute the fraction of its expressed isoforms that are differentially used (`n_sig / n_iso`) and plot the distribution as a histogram.

```{r}
# 4. Per-gene fraction of significant isoforms histogram (Optional challenge #3 in exercise)
per_gene_frac_GSE173955 <- res_isoforms_GSE173955 |> 
  dplyr::transmute(
    gene_id = groupID,
    isoform_id = featureID,
    sig = !is.na(padj) & padj < alpha_GSE173955
  ) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(gene_id) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_iso = dplyr::n(),
    n_sig = sum(sig),
    frac_sig = n_sig / n_iso
  ) |> 
  dplyr::ungroup() |> 
  dplyr::filter(frac_sig > 0)

frac_plot_GSE173955 <- ggplot(per_gene_frac_GSE173955, aes(x = frac_sig)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#009E73", color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "DEXSeq: Per-Gene Fraction of Significant Isoforms (GSE173955)",
    x = "Fraction of significant isoforms per gene",
    y = "Number of genes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

frac_plot_GSE173955
ggsave(file.path(out_dir_GSE173955, "per_gene_isoform_fraction_GSE173955.png"), plot = frac_plot_GSE173955, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300) 
```

Among affected genes, the fraction of significant isoforms per gene ranges from 0.02 to 0.25, with a modal peak at 0.20 (1 significant isoform out of 5), confirming that differential isoform usage is driven by selective isoform switching rather than uniform shifts across all transcripts of a gene.

### Save Essential Results for Cross-Dataset and DESeq2 Integration

Export the isoform-level and gene-level result tables (`.csv`) required for downstream dataset integration (GSE173955 vs. GSE67333) and functional comparison against `DESeq2` via Over-Representation Analysis (ORA) and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (`fgseaMultilevel`).

```{r}
dir.create(out_dir_GSE173955, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

readr::write_csv(res_isoforms_GSE173955, file.path(out_dir_GSE173955, "DEXSeq_all_isoforms_GSE173955.csv")) 
readr::write_csv(sig_isoforms_GSE173955, file.path(out_dir_GSE173955, "DEXSeq_sig_isoforms_GSE173955.csv")) 
readr::write_csv(res_genes_GSE173955, file.path(out_dir_GSE173955, "DEXSeq_all_genes_GSE173955.csv")) 
readr::write_csv(sig_genes_GSE173955, file.path(out_dir_GSE173955, "DEXSeq_sig_genes_GSE173955.csv"))
```
